conviction_note: Q3 numbers are genuinely new (no pre-release since the 15 July interims), and the company-level evidence leans up: >US$81m of 2026 revenue was already booked by 14 July against FY25's US$80.4m, opex is flat after a May restructuring, and the issuer has said 'ahead of market expectations' on its last two full-year updates. But the FY26 bar is unsourced (no Cavendish number reachable), and this name has sold its beats (FY25 'ahead of expectations' -6.6%, H1 -1.0% after a +7.3% run on the notice day). So abs_move is sized at 7.5 for new numbers on a $0.2m/day stock and p_up sits only at 55; expected = (2x0.55-1)x7.5 = +0.75, a bit below the +1.2 sum of findings because the sell-the-beat history weighs on the sign and not on the findings.

No numeric FY26 guide exists; a statement against 'market expectations' (in line or ahead) and the 2026 booked-revenue figure are likely. Lean ahead/in line given US$81m booked by mid-July vs US$79m by mid-October in 2025, and flat opex; a midterm political ad lift lands mostly in Q4.

findings.finding: By 14 July 2026 Audioboom had already booked more than US$81.0m of 2026 revenue, more than all of FY25 (US$80.4m), against US$79m booked by 15 October in 2025; with H2 historically ~55% of revenue, opex flat after the May headcount cut (53 to 44) and >20% marginal EBITDA conversion, the full-year statement is more likely 'ahead of' than 'below' expectations.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY25 trading update 15 Jan 2026 said adj. EBITDA 'ahead of 2025 market expectations' and the stock fell 6.6% (during the offer period); Q3 2024 update +9.5% (15 Oct 2024); H1 2026 -1.0% after +7.3% on the notice day.
findings.original_quote: More than US$81.0 million of booked revenue for 2026 as of 14 July 2026 - ahead of total 2025 revenue (US$80.4 million), with our seasonally highest-demand period ahead
findings.why_not_priced: The booked figure is public, so the finding is only about how the release frames it against a broker bar nobody outside Cavendish's clients can see. The stock is 501p, below the 540p pre-offer price that all three rejected indicative bids were a premium to, and flat on 60 days (+6.6%) - not the chart of a name already priced for an upgrade. With one broker and $0.2m/day of turnover there is no consensus spread to absorb a 'materially ahead' line.
findings.independence: Prior-year comparator from a different document: Q3 2025 update said >US$79.0m booked for 2025 'with 11 weeks of the year remaining' https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/audioboom-group--boom/q3-trading-update/9171313

findings.finding: Counterparty and industry demand stayed strong after Audioboom last spoke: iHeartMedia, the #1 US podcast publisher, reported Q2 podcast revenue +20.7% and guided Q3 consolidated revenue up mid-single digits, and Magellan AI puts H1 2026 political podcast ad spend +42%, which feeds Audioboom's >500m monthly political/news impressions (Crooked Media, The Bulwark, AP).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Audioboom print turned on an industry read-across; Q3 2025 (+9% revenue) fell 9.4% in the offer period, so not comparable.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission, so small: the read-across is public but the market for a one-broker AIM name does not mark it to peer prints; the share price did not move on iHeart's August release beyond the August drift. If priced, BOOM would have re-rated toward the offer premium rather than sitting below 540p.
findings.independence: Political podcast spend +42% H1 2026 (Magellan AI) reported at https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/business/political-podcast-ad-spending-tv-news-youtube/

findings.finding: The up-to-US$10m HSBC revolving credit facility that the 15 July interims said was 'expected to complete in the coming weeks' has had no completion RNS in the three months since (Investegate list shows none), so the Q3 update will either confirm it as M&A firepower or explain a delay.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2025 placing to fund Adelicious (proposed acquisition and £3.0m placing) was followed by a rally; no RCF precedent.
findings.original_quote: the Company has reached agreement in principle with HSBC on a new revolving credit facility of up to US$10.0 million to support the Group's growth strategy, with the facility expected to complete in the coming weeks
findings.why_not_priced: What the money buys is acquisitions toward the US$200m/US$40m 2030 target; a signed facility is mildly positive, a quiet delay mildly negative, and nobody has written about the gap. Near zero net, filed because it is a sourced, open item that resolves in the release.

findings.finding: The stock ran +3.3% into the print on the session after the notice (485p on 9 Oct to 501p intraday 13 Oct) on above-average volume, the same pattern as the interims, when it rose 7.3% on the notice day (14 July) and then fell 1.0% on the record H1 numbers and faded to 432p within three weeks.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Notice-day run then sell on results: 14 Jul 2026 +7.3%, 15 Jul -1.0%, 17 Jul -3.1%; FY25 'ahead of expectations' -6.6% on the day and -17% over three sessions.
findings.why_not_priced: It is the price itself, so this is a reaction-function finding, not information: some of a good number is being bought ahead of the release by a retail-heavy holder base. Small because a 3% run is modest against a 7.5% scale.
findings.independence: Same tape shows the July pattern; no separate source.
